title: Vendor Security Representation and Operational SLA Exhibit
content:
Purpose and scope
This Exhibit is intended to be attached to (and incorporated into) the Master Services Agreement ("MSA") between the Parties. It records the Vendor's security representations and a narrowly-scoped operational SLA tailored to inference service operations, telemetry handling, and artifact handback for customers running sensitive or regulated workloads.

Definitions (capitalized terms)
- "Customer Data": any input, prompt, query, or other data supplied by Customer to the Vendor for processing by inference services.
- "Ephemeral Telemetry": short-lived runtime telemetry (metrics, traces, sampling of non-persistent request headers) used for performance analysis that is not intended to be stored beyond operational needs.
- "Forensic Evidence": preserved logs, snapshots, or artifacts produced in response to a lawful investigation, incident, or audit request.
- "Artifact Handback": the secure delivery of runtime artifacts (encrypted model snapshots, config manifests, or signed container images) to Customer or an independent escrow agent on termination or per the contract schedule.

Vendor security representations and warranties
1) Data handling. Vendor represents that during the Term it will process Customer Data only as necessary to provide the Services and will not use Customer Data to improve or retrain models except where expressly authorized in writing. Any such authorized use will be subject to separate agreement and documented processes.

2) Access controls. Vendor will enforce role-based access controls and MFA for all engineer and operator access to production inference clusters, key management consoles, and audit log stores. Access provisioning and deprovisioning changes will be tracked and available for review for a minimum of twelve (12) months.

3) Cryptographic controls. Data in transit and at rest shall be protected using industry-standard cryptography (TLS 1.2+ for transit; AES-256 or equivalent for storage). Where Customer requires separate key control, Vendor will integrate with the Customer's KMS/HSM via standard protocols (KMIP, cloud-KMS integration) per the Private Deployment Addendum.

4) Signed artifacts. All production container images, model weight bundles, and bootstrap binaries will be signed and provenance recorded. The Vendor will produce a signed manifest for any delivered Artifact Handback.

Operational SLA (applicable modules)
5) Availability targets. For dedicated inference pools covered by a Reserved Capacity schedule, Vendor commits to a monthly availability of 99.9% for the inference request path (excluding scheduled maintenance windows). Availability is measured as successful request path responses over total requests for the SLA scope.

6) Maintenance windows and advance notice. Vendor may perform scheduled maintenance up to 6 hours per calendar month; Customer will be provided at least 72 hours' advance notice for maintenance likely to impact latency or availability. Emergency maintenance will be notified within 2 hours of decision with follow-up RCA.

7) Performance baselines and regression protection. Vendor will maintain per-model baseline latency and tail-latency percentiles (P50, P95, P99) and will not push configuration or kernel changes that degrade any published baseline by >20% without a canary/A-B rollout and rollback plan.

Incident response, telemetry and forensics
8) Incident notification timeline. For any incident that materially affects availability or exposes Customer Data, Vendor will: (a) acknowledge within 1 hour; (b) provide an initial incident summary within 6 hours; and (c) deliver a preliminary mitigation plan within 24 hours. Root cause analysis and final report will be provided within 14 days or a timeline agreed with Customer for complex investigations.

9) Ephemeral telemetry policy. Vendor will collect Ephemeral Telemetry only for performance, stability, and security purposes. By default, Ephemeral Telemetry will be retained for no more than 30 days. When higher retention is required for forensic or compliance reasons, the Vendor will obtain written Customer authorization and segregate retained telemetry into an access-controlled, auditable store with retention and deletion schedules aligned to the agreement.

10) Sampling and minimization. Vendor will implement workload-aware sampling for traces and request-level telemetry to minimize exposure of raw Customer Data. Sampling rules will bias toward error cases and anomalous latency events. Vendor will document sampling heuristics and make them available to Customer under NDA if requested.

11) Forensic evidence preservation. Upon Customer request or in connection with a security incident, Vendor will preserve relevant Forensic Evidence for a reasonable period (minimum 90 days) and make it available for secure transfer or remote review. Requests for forensic exports must be accompanied by lawful justification; Vendor will comply with valid legal process subject to applicable law and its own legal obligations.

Artifact handback, escrow and rollback rights
12) Artifact handback. On expiration or termination for convenience, or on Customer's written request during the Term (subject to fees), Vendor will provide Artifact Handback packages containing signed manifests, model weights (if Customer provided), runtime configs, and a reproducible deployment recipe sufficient to bootstrap a compatible runtime. Delivery format and transfer mechanism will be agreed in the SOW (SFTP, signed container registry transfer, or encrypted archive via KMS).

13) Rollback and freeze window. For production-impacting changes to model variants, kernel selection, or runtime defaults, Customer may request a temporary freeze on rollouts for a mutually-agreed period (not to exceed 30 days absent written extension). Vendor will provide rollback artifacts and procedures to revert to the previous certified configuration within the SLA windows defined above.

Audit rights and evidence scope
14) Rights to audit. Customer has the right to perform a remote audit (document review, access log sampling) once per Contract Year at Customer's expense. Onsite audits will be handled by exception and require 60 days' notice; Vendor may require a redacted evidence set or auditor NDA.

15) Evidence granularity. Audit evidence will include access logs (user, action, resource, timestamp), change control records for production configuration, signed artifact manifests, and a sample of anonymized telemetry demonstrating compliance with sampling and retention commitments. Personal data fields will be redacted unless the Customer provides lawful basis and technical justification for unredacted access.

Liability, limitations and remedies
16) Limitation of liability. Except for indemnities related to breach of data protection obligations or willful misconduct, each Party's aggregate liability for direct damages shall be capped at the greater of (a) fees paid under the affected SOW in the prior 12 months, or (b) USD 1,000,000. Consequential damages remain disclaimed except to the extent prohibited by law.

17) Service credits. For SLA failures within the scope of the Operational SLA (availability target misses), Service Credits will be calculated as a percentage of monthly fees for the affected service tier per the credit schedule in the SOW. Credits are Customer's sole financial remedy for SLA failures.

Data privacy and regulatory cooperation
18) Data subject requests and deletion. Vendor will, upon Customer instruction, assist in responding to data subject requests that relate to Customer Data processed by Vendor. Vendor will follow Customer's retention/deletion schedules for Customer Data and will provide export and deletion proof upon request (hash-based deletion attestations, deletion logs).

19) Regulatory support. Vendor will cooperate with Customer for regulatory inquiries (e.g., data protection authorities) to the extent permitted by law and consistent with the MSA. Cooperation may include preservation of evidence, joint response coordination, and provision of compliance artifacts. Any extraordinary cost associated with such cooperation will be mutually agreed.

Operational requirements and change controls
20) Change control procedures. All operational changes that could affect the security posture, telemetry collection, or artifact signing will follow the Vendor's change control process: documented proposal, risk assessment, canary rollout plan, and rollback procedure. High-risk changes require Customer notice 7 days before canary and a documented remediation path.

21) Developer debug access. Vendor will implement a just-in-time, time-limited debug access model for engineers that is auditable and requires pre-approved justification. Persistent developer accounts into Customer's production environments are prohibited unless explicitly approved via a separate SOW.

Confidentiality and public communications
22) Communication constraints. Vendor will not reference Customer-specific performance statistics, configurations, or security arrangements in marketing or case studies without Customer's prior written consent. Routine performance benchmarks on anonymized workloads remain permitted.

Sign-off
This Exhibit is intended to be an operationally-focused complement to the MSA and DPA. Where conflicts arise between this Exhibit and any other contract module, the order of precedence in the MSA will determine priority unless explicitly amended.
